topic: Fundamentals of Linear Algebra: Vectors in Motion
target_audience: High school students or introductory university students

sections.title: Defining the Vector: Magnitude and Direction
lecture_lines: Scalars are simple numbers like five meters.
Vectors represent both magnitude and direction.
animations: Create a bold arrow from origin (0,0,0); color: #FFFFFF.
Display arrow length with dimension line; color: #FFD700.
Highlight arrow head with bright dot; color: #FF4500.

sections.title: Visualization via Coordinate Systems
lecture_lines: Place the vector on a Cartesian plane.
Define components as horizontal and vertical steps.
animations: Place the vector on the grid at (0,0); color: #FFFFFF.
Draw dashed lines from vector tip to axes; color: #00BFFF.

sections.title: Vector Addition: The Tip-to-Tail Rule
lecture_lines: Connect vectors using the tip-to-tail rule.
The resultant is the path from start to finish.
A boat path diverted by current.
animations: Create a primary vector from origin; color: #FFFFFF.
Translate second vector tail to first tip; color: #FFD700.
Draw resultant from origin to second tip; color: #FF4500.

sections.title: Scalar Multiplication: Scaling Reality
lecture_lines: Scalars scale a vector's total length.
Direction remains constant for positive scalars.
A superhero jump: double length, same direction.
animations: Create base vector along X-axis; color: #FFFFFF.
Double vector length for scalar 2; color: #FFD700.

sections.title: Summary and Real-World Application
lecture_lines: Vectors simplify movement in physics simulations.
Game characters use these for jumping.
animations: Fade in previous vector examples; color: #FFFFFF.
